chunks: Uthman ibn 'Isa narrated from Ibn Maskan, from Abū Baṣīr who said:
I heard Abā Ja'far (peace be upon him) say: 'Verily, a group will be burnt in the Fire until when they become coal-black (humam), they attain intercession.'

Then they will be taken to a river that flows from the perspiration of the inhabitants of Paradise, so they will bathe therein, their flesh and blood will grow back, and the scorching of the Fire will be removed from them. They will enter Paradise and will be called al-Jahannamiyyūn (the inmates of the Fire).
Together, they will cry out: 'O Allah, remove from us this name!'
So He will remove it from them.
Then he said: 'O Abā Baṣīr, verily the enemies of 'Alī will remain in the Fire forever, they will not attain intercession.'

key_terms.الْجَهَنَمِيُّونَ: The inmates of the Fire (a specific title for those exiting Hell)
key_terms.رَشْحُ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ: Perspiration of the inhabitants of Paradise
key_terms.قَشَفُ النَّارِ: The scorching/burning effect of the Fire

ai.seo_question: Who will be removed from Hellfire through intercession and who will remain there eternally?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Shia doctrine of 'Khuruj min al-Nar' (exit from Hell), distinguishing between temporary punishment for the monotheistic sinners who attain intercession and eternal abode for the specific enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt. The imagery of bathing in a river from the perspiration of Paradise highlights the mercy of Allah, while the retention of the name 'al-Jahannamiyyūn' signifies a lasting, albeit non-punitive, mark of their trial. This contrasts with the absolute permanence of the 'A'da' (enemies), underscoring the centrality of Walayah in determining one's ultimate fate.
